html:
SMTO-EXE-0032 — A step needs a result that isn't ready yet

GUID: e15d10c2-4fa3-4cd6-9271-4b0f89847f18
Slug: input-binding-not-completed
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: exe

What happened

  • SMTO tried to use the answer from an earlier step before that step had finished, or tried to chain results inside one combined command. The waiting step did not run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Look through the task's steps for one that is still running or waiting, and let it finish or answer what it is waiting for. The later step can only use a result once the earlier step has finished and saved it.
  2. If the task stops, ask SMTO in the conversation to run the steps one at a time and wait for each result before starting the next. Running steps separately lets each one use the saved result of the step before it.
  3. Give it time instead of sending the same request again and again. Repeating the request quickly can't make the earlier step finish any sooner.

What success looks like

  • The earlier step shows as completed and the next step runs using its result.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the conversation name, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't start the earlier step again by hand; it may already be running.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A tool call bound an input to an activity that has not produced a completed receipt yet, or a shell sequence step used a prior-result marker ("${step", "previous_result" or "source_pointer") that sequences cannot interpolate.

What this means

  • Dependency admission found a binding to a future or unfinished activity instead of an available receipt; shell-sequence preflight also rejects recognizable prior-result interpolation markers because it has no interpolation engine. Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.

Why this can happen

  • Dependency admission found a binding to a future or unfinished activity instead of an available receipt; shell-sequence preflight also rejects recognizable prior-result interpolation markers because it has no interpolation engine.

How to diagnose it

  • Determine whether the failure is an unfinished producer reference or an unsupported sequence marker; inspect actual completed receipt IDs.

How to fix it

  • Let the producing activity reach a completed receipt, then bind its exact operation ID in a separate call's input_bindings (agent_runtime.native.dependency_graph.validate_batch). For shell sequences, split steps that need earlier output into separate calls with input bindings instead of ${step...}/previous_result markers (agent_runtime.native.shell_sequence.execute_sequence).
  • Wait for a required producer, then use its exact receipt in a supported bound-input call. Split sequence steps that require earlier results into separate supported calls.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A separate consumer binds an existing completed producer receipt through the supported input-binding contract.

What not to do

  • Do not use a rapid retry loop or replay an uncertain mutation while waiting for the stated condition.

Technical notes

  • Execution, resource reconciliation and retries remain owned by the existing control flow. Use retained per-operation facts to distinguish this request from earlier effects; this explanation performs no additional work.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
